scope: Cross-branch stock leak, unauthorized decrement vectors, BranchScope coverage

findings.title: BranchScope global on StockLevel + StockMovement closes cross-tenant leak — verified
findings.evidence: StockLevel::boot() line 25 + StockMovement::boot() line 23 both register BranchScope. BranchScope::apply() filters queries by branch_id when (web context OR phpunit tests) AND Auth::check(). Admin (branch_id=0) bypass preserved. StockService queries explicitly add WHERE branch_id (lines 87-89, 391-393) which is REDUNDANT with the global scope but provides defense-in-depth. ChoiceAvailabilityResolver does the same (line 216).
findings.impact: Cross-tenant stock leak NOT exploitable via Eloquent queries. A multi-branch admin user could not see Branch B's stock_levels through Branch A's POS UI.
findings.recommendation: Add a regression test under tests/Feature/Multitenant/ asserting that a staff (branch_id=1) querying StockLevel::all() returns ONLY branch_id=1 rows. Currently StockBranchIsolationTest only tests the forBranch scope helper, not the global BranchScope guard.
findings.heal_reason: No code change needed -- the gap is missing test coverage. Add to V1.0.1 sentinels.

findings.title: Raw DB::table queries bypass BranchScope in AvailabilityService::releaseForOrderItems
findings.evidence: AvailabilityService.php line 630 uses DB::table('order_items')->where('id', $orderItemId)->lockForUpdate()->first() -- this BYPASSES the OrderItem BranchScope. The function then validates item_id AND branch_id from the line item match the DB row (lines 644-654), so a forged $orderItemId pointing to another branch's order_item would be REJECTED with 'availability release skipped (line item mismatch)' log. SAFE in practice.
findings.impact: If a future caller passes attacker-controlled order_item_id values, the line_item_mismatch guard catches them. Cross-branch release attack vector is closed by the (item_id + branch_id) double-key check.
findings.recommendation: Document the implicit security contract: callers MUST supply item_id and branch_id matched against the order_item_id payload. Consider adding a phpunit test asserting cross-branch release IS rejected (currently only the warning log proves it, no assertion). Add to V1.0.1 sentinel suite.
findings.heal_reason: AvailabilityService.php = Menu service, not in our intersection scope mandate. Defer.

findings.title: No HTTP-level authorization gate documented for stock decrement entry points
findings.evidence: Stock decrement is only triggered via OrderCreated/OrderCanceled/RefundCreated events. There is NO HTTP endpoint allowing direct stock manipulation (verified via grep on app/Http/Controllers/). The Spatie permission 'settings' gates StockRuptureDashboardController (admin manual toggle), but that goes through AvailabilityService::toggleExtra/toggleVariation, not the order-driven decrement path. POS submit goes through PosOrderRequest -> OrderService.posStore which requires Auth::check() (POS staff session).
findings.impact: No direct stock-tampering attack surface via HTTP. The only way to mutate stock is via legitimate order submission, which requires authenticated session + branch context.
findings.recommendation: Add a sentinel test asserting NO HTTP route allows direct StockService::decrementForOrder or releaseForOrder calls (currently a grep test would suffice). Add to V1.0.1.

findings.title: StockMovement append-only DB triggers landed but TRUNCATE bypass not REVOKE-ed in prod doc
findings.evidence: Migration 2026_05_18_140000_add_stock_movements_immutability_triggers.php lines 54-55 (comment): 'TRUNCATE TABLE stock_movements bypasses MySQL triggers — mitigation = REVOKE TRUNCATE on prod DB user (deploy doc scope, not migration).' Same caveat as audit_logs/z_reports immutability migrations. The doc note is correct but easily missed.
findings.impact: If a prod DB user has TRUNCATE grant (default in many MySQL installs since TRUNCATE counts as DROP+CREATE), a malicious or compromised user could wipe stock_movements bypassing triggers. Audit trail loss.
findings.recommendation: Add a deploy-doc gate documented in docs/PRODUCTION_DEPLOYMENT_CHECKLIST.md (or equivalent): REVOKE DROP, ALTER, CREATE on `stock_movements` from app DB user; only DBA role gets TRUNCATE. Defense-in-depth same pattern as audit_logs/z_reports. V1.0.1 deploy hardening.
findings.heal_reason: Deploy doc concern, not code-level fix.

findings.title: Idempotency key namespace 'stock:' + sha1 — deterministic, no collision vector
findings.evidence: StockService::movementKey lines 327-344: keys are 'stock:' + sha1(reason | order_class | order_id | line_uid | stockable_type | stockable_id). For order_created reason, $seed is NEVER appended -- so the inline call at OrderService:894 (with seed) and the listener call (without seed) produce identical keys, ensuring single decrement. Cryptographically resistant collision space ~2^160.
findings.impact: Positive -- key construction is deterministic and unforgeable across attempts.

verdict: SECURITY POSTURE OK FOR V1 - 0 P0, 1 P1 (no HTTP route audit sentinel), 3 P2 (test/deploy-doc gaps)
summary: Stock mutation is event-only, no direct HTTP attack surface. BranchScope global on StockLevel + StockMovement closes cross-tenant leak. ChoiceAvailabilityResolver applies explicit branch_id filter. The migration 2026_05_18_140000 closes the raw-query DB-level bypass that was the only remaining vector. Three P2 items are test/deploy-doc completeness items (TRUNCATE REVOKE doc, BranchScope sentinel, no-direct-HTTP-stock sentinel). All deferrable to V1.0.1.
